source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: Reaction distance is the distance traveled from the moment you see danger until you step on the brake and braking distance is the distance traveled from the time the brakes are applied until the vehicle stops and braking distance is much longer on wet icy or gravel roads.
corrections.note: Removed only because no page says reaction distance does not change.

corrections.corrected_statement: A left turn sets up within one foot of the centerline, whereas a right turn sets up about three feet from the right edge of the road.
corrections.note: Left turn setup is stated on the prior page, not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Alternately flashing yellow lights on a school bus mean prepare to stop, while alternately flashing red lights mean you must be stopped.
corrections.note: Yellow-light prepare-to-stop rule is on page 40, not page 41.

corrections.corrected_statement: A pedestrian without a sidewalk walks on the left facing traffic, the opposite of a bicyclist, who rides on the right with traffic.
corrections.note: Bicyclist ride-on-right rule is on page 42, not page 40.

corrections.corrected_statement: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights look ahead toward the right edge of the highway until the bright lights pass and your vision returns, a habit that also helps you spot bicyclists or pedestrians near the road edge.
corrections.note: Key phrase is on page 50, not the cited page 51.

corrections.corrected_statement: If the line to your right on a divided highway is yellow you are going the wrong way and the line to your right should be white.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim that yellow belongs on the left.

corrections.corrected_statement: A truck driver backing up may have to block the street temporarily to maneuver the trailer, and you must never go around a truck that is preparing to back or is backing, because trailers hide objects and you would enter a blind spot.
corrections.note: The blind spot consequence is printed on the next page, not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: A truck's rear no-zone hides you from the driver and hides traffic from you, while its side no-zones are where a sudden truck lane change can hit you; the mirror test applies to both.
corrections.note: The mirror test for all no-zones is printed on the previous page.

corrections.corrected_statement: A slow moving vehicle such as a tractor or other large farm machinery is identified by an orange and red triangular sign mounted on the rear of the vehicle.
corrections.note: Removed the orange diamond work zone claim not stated on provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: A new resident has sixty days to register a vehicle, while a sale paperwork package after a trade must be mailed within twenty-four hours and a name, address or color change must be reported within thirty days.
corrections.note: The thirty-day name address color notice is on page 67, not page 66.

corrections.corrected_statement: Warning signs are usually diamond shaped and yellow or green, and the triangle with cut off points is displayed on vehicles that travel at slow speeds such as farm vehicles.
corrections.note: Removed not on a post and added usually and displayed on vehicles.

corrections.corrected_statement: A regulatory sign is a white rectangle that states a rule, whereas a warning sign is a yellow diamond that flags a danger, and the shape alone tells them apart when the face is obscured.
corrections.note: Same statement is stated on pdf page 33 not pdf page 35.

corrections.corrected_statement: Work zone signs are orange and diamond or rectangular shaped and warn of hazards ahead, and a flagger has the legal authority to control traffic and must be obeyed.
corrections.note: Removed temporary and permanent contrast not stated on the page.

corrections.corrected_statement: If your vehicle stalls in a flooded area abandon it as soon as possible because flood waters can rise rapidly and sweep away a car and its occupants and as little as four inches of water can make it difficult to walk and can hide hazards from view.
corrections.note: Changed knock a walker down to make it difficult to walk.

corrections.corrected_statement: The clock rule puts headlights on from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, while the visibility rule requires them any time persons or vehicles cannot be seen five hundred feet ahead.
corrections.note: Visibility rule is stated on page 47, not page 50.

corrections.corrected_statement: Four wheel and all wheel drive give better traction in snow but no advantage on ice, which is why the winter following distance rises above four seconds for every vehicle.
corrections.note: Better traction in snow is stated on page 49, not page 48.

corrections.corrected_statement: Refusing the implied consent test costs the license for at least six months on its own, separate from any penalty for a driving under the influence conviction.

Only time at a rate of at least one hour per drink reduces the effects of alcohol, and drinking coffee, taking a shower, or exercising cannot reduce blood alcohol concentration or the effects of alcohol.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim that remedies only affect wakefulness.
